---
title: MetaCheck Report
subtitle: "%s"
output:
  html_document:
    theme: null
    highlight: null
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
    toc_float: false
    section_divs: true
    anchor_sections: false
    self_contained: true
    mathjax: null
    md_extensions: "+fenced_divs+header_attributes+bracketed_spans"
---

<style>
  /* A plain-Pandoc page gets none of Bootstrap's layout for free (no
     container, no gutters, no font stack) -- without this, text sets in
     the browser's bare serif default at full window width, and the old
     `h2, h3 { margin-left: -20px }` (copied from the full report, where
     Quarto's own container absorbs it) had nothing to push against and
     ran headings off the left edge instead. Everything below is plain
     CSS3, inline in the page -- no external stylesheet or font request,
     so the report stays a single, self-contained file safe to email.

     Visual language is a bank/financial-statement one (full-bleed colour
     banner, bold rule-separated summary rows, tinted alternating table
     rows) per the user's own reference screenshots -- restyled in
     Metacheck's own brand green rather than copying their orange. */
  :root {
    color-scheme: light;
    --mc-ink: #1a1a1a;
    --mc-muted: #5b6b66;
    --mc-brand: #15342A;
    --mc-brand-light: #1f4a3b;
    --mc-accent: #c9a35f;
    --mc-border: #d8dee2;
    --mc-bg-soft: #f6f7f7;
    --mc-bg-tint: #eef3f1;
  }
  html { color-scheme: light; }
  body {
    margin: 0;
    padding: 0;
    font-family: -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial,
      sans-serif;
    font-size: 16px;
    line-height: 1.6;
    color: var(--mc-ink);
    background: #ffffff;
  }
  /* Pandoc's own auto-generated title block is replaced below by the
     banner -- hidden rather than removed from the YAML, since title/
     subtitle still set the HTML <title> tag. rmarkdown's default HTML
     template emits this as bare h1.title/h3.subtitle siblings directly in
     <body> (confirmed in the rendered output), NOT wrapped in a `#header`
     element the way the old `#header { display: none }` selector assumed
     -- that selector matched nothing, so both the plain Pandoc title block
     AND the banner below rendered, one after the other. */
  h1.title.toc-ignore, h3.subtitle { display: none; }
  .mc-banner {
    position: relative;
    background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--mc-brand) 0%, var(--mc-brand-light) 100%);
    color: #ffffff;
    padding: 2.6em 1.5em 2.2em;
    margin-bottom: 0;
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  /* Dot-pattern texture in the top-right corner, per the user's own
     reference screenshots -- a repeating radial-gradient (no external
     image, so the report stays a single self-contained file), masked to a
     soft-edged circle so it reads as a decorative accent, not a hard-edged
     tile. */
  .mc-banner::before {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    top: -3em;
    right: -3em;
    width: 16em;
    height: 16em;
    background-image: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(255,255,255,0.35) 1.5px, transparent 1.5px);
    background-size: 10px 10px;
    -webkit-mask-image: radial-gradient(circle at 70% 30%, #000 0%, #000 45%, transparent 72%);
    mask-image: radial-gradient(circle at 70% 30%, #000 0%, #000 45%, transparent 72%);
    pointer-events: none;
  }
  .mc-banner-inner {
    position: relative;
    max-width: 50em;
    margin: 0 auto;
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 1.3em;
  }
  .mc-banner img { width: 4.2em; height: 4.2em; flex-shrink: 0; }
  .mc-banner h1.title {
    font-size: 2.1em;
    font-weight: 600;
    color: #ffffff;
    margin: 0 0 0.15em;
    letter-spacing: -0.01em;
  }
  .mc-banner .subtitle {
    font-size: 1.1em;
    color: #d9e6e0;
    font-weight: normal;
    margin: 0;
  }
  .mc-page {
    max-width: 50em;
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 2em 1.5em 4em;
  }
  h1, h2, h3, h4, h5 { line-height: 1.3; color: var(--mc-ink); }
  h2 {
    font-size: 1.35em;
    font-weight: 600;
    margin-top: 2.2em;
    padding-bottom: 0.4em;
    border-bottom: 2px solid var(--mc-brand);
  }
  h3 { font-size: 1.1em; margin-top: 1.6em; }
  h4 {
    font-size: 0.85em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    letter-spacing: 0.04em;
    color: var(--mc-brand);
    margin-top: 1.6em;
    font-weight: 700;
  }
  h5 { font-size: 1em; font-style: italic; margin-top: 1.1em; }
  p { margin: 0.8em 0; }
  a { color: var(--mc-brand-light); }
  ul, ol { padding-left: 1.4em; }
  li { margin-bottom: 0.3em; }
  hr { border: none; border-top: 1px solid var(--mc-border); margin: 2em 0; }
  #TOC {
    border: 1px solid var(--mc-border);
    border-left: 4px solid var(--mc-brand);
    border-radius: 0.3em;
    padding: 1em 1.5em;
    margin-bottom: 2em;
    background: var(--mc-bg-soft);
  }
  #TOC ul { padding-left: 1.2em; }
  .emoji-key {
    list-style: none;
    padding: 0.9em 1.3em;
    margin: 0 0 1.8em;
    border: 1px solid var(--mc-border);
    border-radius: 0.3em;
    background: var(--mc-bg-soft);
    display: flex;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 0.3em 1.5em;
  }
  .emoji-key li { margin: 0; font-size: 0.92em; white-space: nowrap; }
  /* Summary module list, ledger-row style (per the user's own reference
     screenshots): each module is a row with a left colour stripe for its
     status, icon, title and one-line result -- thin rule between rows
     rather than a plain bulleted list, which previously gave every row
     identical markup regardless of red/yellow/green status. */
  ul.mc-summary {
    list-style: none;
    padding: 0;
    margin: 0 0 1.5em;
    border: 1px solid var(--mc-border);
    border-radius: 0.3em;
    overflow: hidden;
  }
  li.mc-summary-row {
    display: flex;
    align-items: flex-start;
    gap: 0.8em;
    padding: 0.8em 1em;
    margin: 0;
    border-left: 4px solid var(--mc-border);
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--mc-border);
    background: #ffffff;
  }
  ul.mc-summary > li.mc-summary-row:last-child { border-bottom: none; }
  li.mc-summary-row.red { border-left-color: #a4282f; background: #fdf4f4; }
  li.mc-summary-row.yellow { border-left-color: #a67c1f; background: #fdf9ef; }
  li.mc-summary-row.green { border-left-color: var(--mc-brand); }
  li.mc-summary-row.fail { border-left-color: #a4282f; background: #fdf4f4; }
  li.mc-summary-row.info { border-left-color: #4a7a9c; }
  li.mc-summary-row.na { border-left-color: var(--mc-border); }
  .mc-summary-icon { font-size: 1.1em; line-height: 1.5; flex-shrink: 0; }
  .mc-summary-body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-width: 0; }
  .mc-summary-title { font-weight: 700; color: var(--mc-ink); }
  .mc-summary-title a { color: inherit; text-decoration: none; }
  .mc-summary-title a:hover { text-decoration: underline; }
  .mc-summary-text { color: var(--mc-muted); font-size: 0.95em; }
  /* To-do bullets for a flagged module (brief mode only) -- a normal
     markdown list that sits visually under its row via indent + a thin
     left guide rule, without being nested inside the row's own raw HTML
     <li> (Pandoc cannot markdown-process **bold**/links nested inside raw
     HTML -- see report.R's own comment on why this stays a sibling block). */
  .mc-summary-todo {
    margin: -0.6em 0 1.1em 2.6em;
    padding: 0.2em 0 0.2em 1em;
    border-left: 2px solid var(--mc-border);
  }
  .mc-summary-todo ul { margin: 0; padding-left: 1.1em; }
  .mc-summary-todo li { font-size: 0.92em; color: var(--mc-ink); margin-bottom: 0.4em; }
  /* Statement-style tables: bold brand header row, a heavier top rule
     under the header (the reference screenshots' thin-rule-per-row
     ledger look), tinted alternating rows instead of boxed-in grid lines. */
  th {
    background-color: var(--mc-brand);
    color: white;
    font-weight: 600;
    font-size: 0.85em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    letter-spacing: 0.03em;
  }
  table.dt-static {
    margin: 1em 0 1.6em;
    width: 100%;
    border-collapse: collapse;
    font-size: 0.95em;
  }
  table.dt-static th, table.dt-static td {
    padding: 0.6em 0.8em;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--mc-border);
    text-align: left;
  }
  table.dt-static th { border-bottom: 2px solid var(--mc-accent); }
  table.dt-static tr:nth-child(even) { background-color: var(--mc-bg-soft); }
  table strong { color: #a4282f; }
  details {
    border: 1px solid var(--mc-border);
    border-left: 4px solid var(--mc-brand);
    border-radius: 0.3em;
    padding: 0.2em 1em;
    margin: 1em 0;
    background: var(--mc-bg-soft);
  }
  summary { color: var(--mc-ink); cursor: pointer; font-weight: 600; padding: 0.5em 0; }
  .callout-note, .callout-tip, .callout-warning, .callout-important, .callout-caution {
    border-left: 4px solid var(--mc-brand);
    border-radius: 0.2em;
    padding: 0.8em 1.2em;
    margin: 1.2em 0;
    background-color: var(--mc-bg-soft);
  }
  .validation {
    display: block;
    border: 1px solid var(--mc-border);
    border-left: 4px solid var(--mc-accent);
    border-radius: 0.3em;
    padding: 1em 1.2em;
    margin-bottom: 1.5em;
    background-color: var(--mc-bg-tint);
  }
  /* Sits on .mc-page's white background (moved out of the dark banner so
     the banner itself stays just logo + title/subtitle, matching the
     reference statement layout) -- coloured for that light background,
     not the near-white-on-white left over from when this block used to
     render inside the banner. */
  #info {
    font-size: 0.85em;
    color: var(--mc-muted);
    text-align: right;
    margin: 0 0 1.8em;
    padding-bottom: 0.8em;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--mc-border);
  }
  #info a { color: var(--mc-brand-light); }
  /* Brief mode's combined version/date/DOI + legend box (see report.R's
     own info_box) -- a real, still-used element, NOT superseded by
     .emoji-key: that only replaces the full report's standalone legend
     list, which brief mode never emits in the first place. */
  .legend {
    font-size: 0.9em;
    color: var(--mc-muted);
    padding: 0.8em 1.2em;
    border: 1px solid var(--mc-border);
    border-left: 4px solid var(--mc-brand);
    border-radius: 0.3em;
    background: var(--mc-bg-soft);
    margin-bottom: 1.5em;
  }
  .legend p { margin: 0.2em 0; }
  .legend hr { margin: 0.6em 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--mc-border); }
</style>

<div class="mc-banner">
<div class="mc-banner-inner">
<img src="{{LOGO_DATA_URI}}" alt="MetaCheck logo">
<div>
<h1 class="title">MetaCheck Report</h1>
<p class="subtitle">%s</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<!-- End Banner -->

<div class="mc-page">

::: {#info}
[MetaCheck](http://www.scienceverse.org/metacheck) version %s \
Report Created: %s \
%s <!-- doi, if exists -->
:::

This is a **simple** report: a static, email-safe version with no interactive tables, tabs, or theme switching, and no embedded JavaScript, so that mail clients and scanners do not flag it as active content.

<ul class="emoji-key">
  <li class="red">⚠️ possible problems detected</li>
  <li class="yellow">🔍 something to check</li>
  <li class="green">✅️ no problems detected</li>
  <li class="info">ℹ️ informational only</li>
  <li class="na">⬜ not applicable</li>
  <li class="fail">☠️ check failed</li>
</ul>

[Metacheck](https://www.scienceverse.org/metacheck/) is a tool that screens scientific manuscripts and aims to identify potential issues for improvement. Our goal is to guide researchers towards best practices, especially with respect to practices that researchers easily forget, or might not have learned about yet. Metacheck is developed to help researchers correctly and completely report statistical results, will point to possibly relevant information about citations, and provides feedback about data and code sharing.

Metacheck combines existing and new checks in a module-based tool. It is open source, and anyone can contribute modules. It mainly relies on text search or retrieving information from external sources through API’s or web-scraping, but the power modules can optionally use large language models. The use of LLM's is always optional and opt-in. The development of Metacheck is guided by our [values statement](https://www.scienceverse.org/metacheck/#our-values).

::: {.validation}
In light with our values, our modules are validated on sets of open-access papers. In each validated module, there will be a sentence explaining the prevalence of false positives (incorrect detection/classification) and false negatives (incorrect omission). For example, if a hypothetical module detects the inappropriate practice of "woozling", the sentence might read:

> In a sample of 250 papers from the *Journal of X*, there were 350 instances of woozling. This module correctly detected 340 of them, and incorrectly identified 7. Therefore 3% of true instances are missed, and 2% of detections are false positives.

There is an inherent tradeoff between false positives and false negatives. Many of our modules are designed like "smoke detectors", where they are more likely to detect a practice that needs attention, but also more likely to incorrectly flag something. Therefore, you need to check the output of each module, keeping the validated error rates in mind.
:::

Metacheck is under continuous development. It can be surprisingly difficult to automatically retrieve information from papers, and there is a large amount of edge-cases where our tool might not yet work accurately. By using our tool, and providing us with feedback about what we can't get right yet, you will help to improve the tool for all other users. Issues can be submitted [on Github](https://github.com/scienceverse/metacheck/issues), and suggestions for improvement or feedback can be sent to [metacheck@scienceverse.org](mailto:metacheck@scienceverse.org).
